extraction.name: FLEURS: Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech
extraction.description: An n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the FLoRes-101 machine translation benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It is intended for evaluating speech recognition, speech language identification, translation, and retrieval, especially in low-resource multilingual settings.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research; Google Research; Carnegie Mellon University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by starting from the FLoRes-101 dataset, splitting the dev and devtest sentences into new train/dev/test splits, and collecting three speech recordings per sentence from three different native speakers. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers for correspondence to the input sentence; invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In the first version of the dataset, about 21.5% of the sentences are missing because none of the three recordings were validated.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentences extracted from English Wikipedia in FLoRes-101, translated into 101 languages by human translators; speech recordings collected for each sentence in 102 languages.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation was performed. The paper states that missing sentences will be filled in future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dev and devtest sets from FLoRes-101 were split into new train, dev, and test splits with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively. Recordings were kept as-is without data augmentations. Text was normalized with NFC and FST normalization, lowercased, punctuation removed, and split into characters; three transcript versions were provided: raw, normalized, and character-based.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid recordings were discarded after validation by additional workers. All segments were constrained to within 30 seconds. For text, NFC and FST normalization were applied, text was lowercased, punctuation removed, and words were split into characters to create SRC NORM and SRC CHAR versions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human translators produced the source transcripts in FLoRes-101. For speech collection, three native speakers recorded each sentence, and additional workers validated whether each recording matched the input sentence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Recordings were validated by additional workers; invalid recordings were discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings per sentence were collected, but after validation the final dataset contains between zero and three recordings per sentence.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three different native speakers per sentence; a balance in sex ratio of at least 30/70% was imposed when possible.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that missing sentences will be filled in future versions of the dataset.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Sex ratio of speakers; native speaker status; language and geographical group information are included.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to catalyze research toward speech technology in more languages and low-resource speech understanding, enabling progress toward speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes imbalance in sex ratio was only enforced when possible. Performance differences across geographical groups are discussed, with better results for Western European languages and worse results for Sub-Saharan African and South Asian languages, partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data for some groups during pretraining.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. The dataset is limited to 102 languages and all segments are within 30 seconds. The paper also notes that some groups, especially CJK and unseen languages, show degraded performance in downstream tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Can be used for Automatic Speech Recognition, Speech Language Identification, Translation, Retrieval, speech-to-text translation, speech-to-speech translation, text-to-text retrieval, speech-to-text retrieval, and text-to-speech retrieval. The paper uses it for baseline training and evaluation on ASR, LangID, and cross-modal retrieval.
